al.2023.0.1.text: Editorial correction: the original prints f: N × N → N, but its recurrence gives f(1,3) = -1. The bank uses the integer codomain Z and positive-integer inputs. The codomain correction is disclosed; this record does not carry an exact-source badge.

atg.2015.0.2.text: Source note: Official English wording "is less or equal 1" rendered as "is less than or equal to 1".

atg.2021.0.3.text: Editorial correction: the official English paper has the German word "und" ("2020 und 2021"); written as "and".

atg.2026.0.3.text: Editorial correction: the official English paper has the German word "und" in the example ("{3} und {1, 3}"); written as "and". The example table is reproduced as a LaTeX array.

at.1970.0.1.text: Editorial correction: the source prints the three factors joined by '+' signs, i.e. $\left(1+\frac1x\right)+\left(1+\frac1y\right)+\left(1+\frac1z\right)\ge 64$, which is false (the minimum of that sum under $x+y+z=1$ is $12$, at $x=y=z=\frac13$). The product form, the well-known version of this inequality with equality at $x=y=z=\frac13$, is printed here.

at.1971.1.3.text: Source ambiguity: the contributed English says 'twice as many direct ways from B to C as from A to B'; it is not clear whether the comparison is with the direct roads or with all routes from A to B. The wording is kept.

at.1971.2.5.text: Editorial correction: the source prints only the bracket $\left[\left(a_1+\frac{a_1a_2}{2}+\cdots+\frac{a_1\cdots a_n}{2^{n-1}}\right)\frac{\pi}{4}\right]$ on the left, with no function applied; as printed the identity is false (for $n=1$, $a_1=1$ it reads $\frac{\pi}{4}=\sqrt2$). The factor $2\sin$ before the bracket, which makes the identity true (for $n=1$: $2\sin\frac{\pi}{4}=\sqrt2$; checked also for $n=2$), was supplied.

at.1972.2.5.text: Editorial correction: the source prints the recursion as $a_n=\frac{a_{n-1}^2}{a_{n-2}}$, in which $C$ does not occur although the hypothesis involves $\frac{A^2+B^2+C}{AB}$; with that recursion the claim is false (e.g. $A=2$, $B=1$, $C=3$ gives $a_3=\frac12$). The recursion $a_n=\frac{a_{n-1}^2+C}{a_{n-2}}$, the well-known form of this problem, is printed here.

at.1974.1.3.text: Source ambiguity: the contributed text ends with 'for each k < 1'. It is unclear whether $k<1$ is a fixed given constant (the inequality required for all $n$) or whether one sequence must work for every $k<1$; the printed wording is kept.

at.1975.2.5.text: Source ambiguity: the contributed text says 'the maximum number of pairs of noncongruent triangles'; it is rendered as 'pairwise non-congruent triangles', the reading consistent with the comparison with the number of all triangles.

at.1976.1.3.text: Source ambiguity: the contributed text says 'Put A = 1976' while the system uses $\alpha$; it is read as $\alpha = 1976$. Whether the angle is meant in degrees or radians is not stated.

at.1977.2.5.text: Source ambiguity: the parameter is defined as $a=\frac{5z}{1+z}$ in terms of the unknown $z$; this is printed as in the source and cannot be checked against the original.

at.1978.1.3.text: Source ambiguity: the hypothesis 'which can be transformed one into another by translations and not by turns around the same point' is rendered as printed; its precise meaning in the original is uncertain.

at.1978.2.5.text: Editorial correction: the source says 'Let f be a constant function'; a constant function cannot have the stated property (it would have to map $A$ into $B$ and $B$ into $A$ with a single value), so 'constant' is a mistranslation of German 'stetig' (continuous) and 'continuous' is printed here.

at.1978.2.6.text: Editorial correction: the contributed text says the projections 'form a square $V_1$' and then constructs $V_2$ 'similarly'. The underlying theorem (the fourth pedal quadrilateral is similar to the original quadrilateral) concerns general quadrilaterals, so 'square' is taken as a mistranslation of German 'Viereck' (quadrilateral) and 'quadrilateral' is printed here.

at.1981.2.5.text: Source ambiguity: the contributed text reads 'For which natural numbers n! divided by $\sum_{i=1}^n i^2$ become larger than 1?'. It is uncertain whether the original asks when the quotient exceeds $1$ (printed here) or, more likely for an olympiad, when $n!$ is divisible by $\sum_{i=1}^n i^2$.

at.1984.1.2.text: Source ambiguity: the domain is $\mathbb{N}_0$, but the equation is quantified over 'all real numbers $x, y$ with $x \ne y$'; presumably $x, y \in \mathbb{N}_0$ with $x > y$ is meant. The printed wording is kept.

at.1987.2.5.text: Source ambiguity: the source (and the identical imomath.com copy) gives the index range only as $1 \le i \le n$; the intended range is presumably all pairs $1 \le i < j \le n$. Kept as printed.

at.1991.2.5.text: Source ambiguity: for $n = 1$ both sides equal $1$, so the strict inequality as printed (also in the identical imomath.com copy) holds only for $n \ge 2$. Kept as printed.

at.1993.2.4.text: Source ambiguity: the quantifier over $m$ is not stated in the source; presumably the identity is required for all natural numbers $k, m$ with $2m \le k \le 3m$.

at.1993.2.5.text: Editorial correction: the source asks for the solutions 'in $\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}$', but the system has three unknowns $x, y, z$; rendered as 'real solutions'. The stacked fractions of the third equation are transcribed as printed.

at.1994.1.3.text: Source ambiguity: the translation says 'not all different from zero' (i.e. at least one of $a, b, c$ is zero); this may be a mistranslation of 'not all equal to zero'. Kept as printed.

at.1994.2.5.text: Source ambiguity: the source refers to the ÖMO logo (not reproduced in the source); the lattice is the ordinary tiling of the plane by unit equilateral triangles. The translation is rough and the intended conditions on the curve (e.g. non-self-intersecting) are not stated.

at.1995.1.1.text: Source ambiguity: the translation reads 'For how much odd or even integer numbers $n$ applies'; rendered as asking for the number of odd and of even such $n$ (presumably positive integers).

at.1995.2.6.text: Source ambiguity: the translation says the cube vertices lie 'in the sides' of the tetrahedron; rendered as 'on the faces' (German 'Seitenflächen').

at.1998.1.2.text: Source ambiguity: parts a)-c) are printed with general $n$; presumably $n = 98$ is intended, as in the last question.

at.2001.1.3.text: Editorial correction: the source writes 'C lies between the lines c = AB and C′', using the capital $C'$ (a vertex name) for the tangent line just introduced as $c'$; printed here as $c'$. Notation only, mathematics unchanged.

at.2003.2.6.text: Editorial correction: the source (and the imomath.com copy) reads 'The tangents to k at A and R meet at R', which is circular since $R$ is the point being defined; by symmetry with 'the tangents at B and P meet at S', the intended point of tangency is $Q$, printed here.

at.2006.1.2.text: Editorial correction: in the contributed PDF the second term is mis-typeset as '[1/3]' followed by $\frac{a^3+b^3+c^3}{3}$ (a broken cube-root sign). The re-typeset copy of the same IMO Compendium text on imomath.com prints $\sqrt[3]{\frac{a^3+b^3+c^3}{3}}$, which is printed here.

at.2009.1.1.text: Source ambiguity: the source labels the tower of $B_k(y)$ with 'm fours' although $B_k$ carries only the index $k$; presumably $k$ fours are intended. The top exponent of $A_{km}(x)$ is printed as $x$ with $\alpha_m$ raised above it and is read here as $x^{\alpha_m}$ (it could also be meant as $x\alpha_m$). Kept as printed.

at.2009.1.2.text: Editorial correction: in part (a) the source prints the denominator as $b-a+a$; this is a misprint for $b-a+1$ (the number of summands, as in part (b), making $M(a,b)$ the arithmetic mean), printed here. Square brackets denote the integer part.

at.2010.1.3.text: Editorial correction: the source says the ball is placed 'on the circumference of the hexagon, but not on one of its edges', which is self-contradictory since the perimeter consists of the edges; this is a mistranslation of German 'Ecken' (corners, i.e. vertices), and 'vertices' is printed here.

at.2014.2.4.text: Editorial correction: the source defines $M(n)$ but then speaks of 'all elements of $N(n)$'; $N(n)$ is undefined and is a misprint for $M(n)$, printed here.

cn.2014.1.1.text: Year convention: this six-problem paper was held in Nanjing on 21–22 December 2013. The coach-authored source labels it 2013, while the English AoPS archive indexes the same paper as China National Olympiad 2014 (collection 5237). The bank retains the existing 2014 edition convention; this does not assert an examination date in calendar 2014.

cn.2015.1.2.text: Source configuration convention: the AoPS compilation says K lies on ST without distinguishing the segment from its supporting line; it supplies no diagram or explicit exclusions for degenerate intersections. The source wording is retained pending primary-source comparison.

cn.2016.1.2.text: Notation expansion: the AoPS statement specifies AK/KB = AD/BC and “its cyclic equivalents”. The other three ratios are displayed explicitly by cycling A, B, C, D. No original figure is present in the uploaded PDF.

cn.2016.1.3.text: Source domain omission: the AoPS compilation does not explicitly state the coefficient domain of P(x). Its wording is retained; an integer-coefficient or finite-field formulation needs confirmation against an original contest source.

cn.2016.2.6.text: Source convention and objective: the AoPS compilation says “complete directed graph” without explicitly defining the orientation convention. It asks for the minimum, not the maximum, of m(G) in part (b). Both are retained literally pending comparison with the original contest paper.

cn.1988.1.2.text: Source extension convention: the book says extensions of the four sides but does not explicitly select between the two intersections of each supporting line with the larger circle. No statement figure is printed. The wording is retained pending original-paper comparison.

cn.1988.2.4.text: Editorial correction: part (b) on printed page 31 omits the outer square on the sum of squares. The bank restores that square, as explicitly used in the book's inductive proof on printed page 114 (scan page 121). The conclusion is expressed for distinct indices, as in that proof. Original-paper confirmation remains pending.

cn.1989.1.2.text: Source domain omission: the book does not explicitly require n ≥ 2, although its formula is undefined for n = 1. The positive-variable sum condition and printed formula are preserved; apply only where the displayed denominators are defined.

cn.1989.2.6.text: Source exponent transcription: the scan prints 1/(4m) and 1/(4n) as the two exponents. They are retained literally; no replacement based on a presumed intended problem has been made.

cn.1990.1.1.text: Source existence omission: the statement refers to a common chord without separately assuming that the circles have two distinct intersections. No extra intersection condition has been silently added.

cn.1990.1.3.text: Unresolved source endpoint error: the hypothesis constrains f only through positive x and y, while the declared domain includes zero. The printed conclusion has no positive-x restriction. For example f(x)=0 for x>0 and f(0)=1 satisfies the hypotheses but fails the conclusion at zero. The record preserves the printed formulation; use its conclusion only for x>0 pending original-paper confirmation.

cn.1993.1.1.text: Editorial correction: the printed statement on page 52 gives the third family as a_i+b_(i+k). The book's construction and proof on pages 181–182 (scan pages 188–189) instead use b_i+b_(i+k). The bank adopts the latter explicitly: at k=0 the printed third family would duplicate the second family. Original-paper confirmation remains pending.

cn.1993.1.3.text: Source configuration omission: the book does not explicitly state convexity or select the direction of each side extension. Its wording is retained; no statement figure is printed and no unverified diagram has been added.

cn.1993.2.4.text: Source resultant convention: the source discusses angles to subset sums without explicitly requiring those sums to be nonzero. The intended angle condition presupposes nonzero resultant vectors; no separate original-paper confirmation is claimed.

cn.1995.1.2.text: Natural-number convention: the AoPS PDF does not state whether zero is included. The recurrence forces f(0)=0 if zero is included; the Chinese compilation uses the same natural-number wording. No convention has been silently selected.

cn.1995.1.3.text: Documented source correction: AoPS restricts x,y to integers, while the Chinese contest-and-solution compilation, scan page 31 (printed 30), states arbitrary real numbers. The bank restores the real-variable domain. No official original-paper certification is claimed.

cn.1995.2.4.text: Source convention: the Chinese compilation calls the further sphere a small sphere; AoPS omits that qualifier. The external-tangency wording is retained; no diagram is printed in the uploaded statement PDF.

cn.1995.2.5.text: Natural-number convention: AoPS and the Chinese contest-and-solution compilation say natural numbers without explicitly defining whether zero is admitted. The Chinese retyped compilation instead says positive integers. The uploaded AoPS wording is retained; this discrepancy remains unresolved.

cn.1996.1.1.text: Documented source correction: the acute-triangle hypothesis omitted by AoPS is restored from the Chinese contest-and-solution compilation, scan page 34. It ensures that the two real tangents in the configuration exist.

cn.1996.2.4.text: Source omission: both compilations omit an explicit positive requirement on m or on the common number of joint appearances. A nonempty festival schedule is presupposed; allowing zero concerts gives a trivial schedule. No unconfirmed condition was silently added.

cn.1999.1.2.text: Reciprocal-domain convention: part (a) uses x inverse and therefore applies for x nonzero, or as a polynomial identity after clearing the reciprocal. The source does not state that restriction separately.

cn.2000.2.4.text: Source variant: AoPS and the Chinese contest-and-solution compilation (scan page 52) ask for the mean of the first entry. The separate Chinese retyped compilation asks for every entry. The uploaded AoPS task is retained.

cn.2000.2.5.text: Documented source correction: the Chinese contest-and-solution compilation, scan page 53, requires every n_i to be greater than 3, whereas AoPS prints greater than or equal to 3. The strict condition is restored. The denominator in the exponent is 2^k, verified visually in both sources.

cn.2001.1.1.text: Documented task restoration: AoPS asks only for the minimum ratio. The Chinese contest-and-solution compilation, scan page 54, asks for both the maximum and minimum; both tasks are restored.

cn.2001.2.6.text: Documented domain restoration: AoPS allows arbitrary integer pairs with n nonzero. The Chinese contest-and-solution compilation, scan page 56, requires positive integer pairs. Positivity is restored rather than retaining an unbounded altered problem.

cn.2002.1.1.text: Documented source correction: undefined angle NDE in AoPS is BDE in the Chinese contest-and-solution compilation, scan page 58, and the Chinese retyped compilation, scan page 33. Both also require E,F strictly inside the side segments. These conditions are restored explicitly.

cn.2002.1.2.text: Typographical repair: the AoPS recurrence has an unmatched opening parenthesis before p_n(x)^2. The balanced recurrence is confirmed on scan page 58 of the Chinese contest-and-solution compilation.

cn.2002.2.4.text: Documented domain restoration: the distinctness of the four points, omitted by AoPS and needed for the denominator, is explicit in the Chinese retyped compilation, scan page 34.

cn.2002.2.5.text: Circle-interior clarification: scan page 61 of the Chinese contest-and-solution compilation says every circle centered at a rational point contains a point of each of the three sets in its interior. This means one point from each set, not exactly three points per set and not points on the circumference.

cn.2007.1.3.text: Documented task correction: AoPS asks for the number of odd operations versus even permutations, although both classes are defined as operations. The Chinese magazine statement embedded on scan page 91 of the contest-and-solution compilation compares even and odd operation groups; the bank uses that comparison. The product definition of parity from AoPS is retained.

cn.2007.2.4.text: Source configuration omission: the sources do not explicitly exclude coincident incenter and circumcenter or parallel defining lines. The displayed construction must exist and the perpendicularity assertion presupposes a defined line OI; no unverified exclusions were added.

cn.2007.2.5.text: Documented source correction: AoPS prints the undefined lower summation index k=a. The Chinese magazine statement on scan page 91 and Mathematical Excalibur 18(3), page 1, both give k=n and a strict inequality. The bank restores k=n. A separate retyped Chinese compilation incorrectly uses equality.

cn.2007.2.6.text: Documented task and domain restoration: AoPS says find a number and does not specify that the a_i are integers. The Chinese magazine statement on scan page 91 requires the smallest integer n at least 9, arbitrary integer a_i, and coefficients in {4,7}. Those omitted conditions are restored.

cn.2008.1.1.text: Documented hypothesis restoration: the Chinese magazine statement on scan page 95 requires an acute scalene triangle, while AoPS omits acute. Its A_1,A_2 projection labels are also adopted; interchanging those two labels does not change the circumradius.

cn.2008.1.2.text: Documented detail restoration: the Chinese magazine statement on scan page 95 explicitly requires both parts of the partition to be nonempty; AoPS omits nonempty.

cn.2008.1.3.text: Unresolved source variant: AoPS assumes equal weighted sums and allows every real alpha. The Chinese magazine instead prints a greater-than-or-equal hypothesis with every real alpha, which is false as stated: n=1, x_1=1, y_1=0, alpha=-1 gives -1 >= 0. The bank retains the consistent equality version of the uploaded AoPS PDF; original-paper confirmation remains pending.

cn.2008.2.4.text: Documented domain restoration: the Chinese magazine statement on scan page 95 specifies n>1, positive integer elements and finitely many distinct elements in the resulting sum. These conditions omitted or abbreviated by AoPS are restored.

cn.2008.2.5.text: Documented trapezoid convention: the Chinese magazine statement on scan page 95 explicitly defines an isosceles trapezoid as having one pair of parallel sides and equal nonparallel sides. Thus rectangles are excluded. This definition is restored; it affects the task.

cn.2008.2.6.text: Documented domain restoration: the Chinese magazine statement on scan page 95 requires n>1; AoPS only says n is positive. The original magazine domain is restored.

cn.1997.1.1.text: Source correction: the English 1996–1997 collection misprints the last exponent as 1/2. Both inspected Chinese compilations print the twelfth power for every variable; this consistent version is retained.

cn.1997.2.5.text: The English collection lists i=1,...,16 and defines an eighteenth entry but does not explicitly print the wraparound difference. Both Chinese compilations explicitly include the difference between the images of 1 and 17. The bank retains this complete cyclic condition, with positive iteration indices.

cn.1997.2.6.text: Source-domain variant: the English collection restricts the sequence to nonnegative integers. Both inspected Chinese compilations say a nonnegative sequence without an integrality restriction. The bank renders this as nonnegative real terms; the bound is valid for that domain.

cn.2017.1.1.text: The inspected Chinese compilation explicitly requires eventual integer terms divisible by u_n; the shorter AoPS transcription omits the integer-term wording. The full condition is retained.

cn.2017.1.2.text: The inspected Chinese statement includes AB>AC, omitted in the AoPS transcription. It also describes P,Q as a diameter through I; the full Chinese condition is retained.

cn.2020.1.1.text: The compilation prints |a_i|-|a_{i+1}|<=1, whereas AoPS prints |a_i-a_{i+1}|<=1. The latter version is retained: the former would allow arbitrarily large alternating terms and invalidate the finite maximum task.

cn.2022.1.3.text: Domain variant: AoPS asks for positive integers a; the inspected Chinese compilation asks for all integers a. The bank retains the positive-integer AoPS version. The condition depends only on a modulo 37.

cn.2023.1.3.text: The Chinese compilation mislabels the white matching using m instead of n. The white matching has n pairs, as required by its 2n white vertices and confirmed by the AoPS paper.

cn.2024.1.1.text: The AoPS public transcription mistakenly lists x_1,...,x_n before a product of 2023 factors. The inspected Chinese paper confirms exactly 2023 positive integer factors.

cn.2024.2.4.text: The bank retains the exact maximum-cardinality question in the inspected Chinese paper; the AoPS reproduction additionally requests equality cases for its stated bound.

cn.2025.1.1.text: The public AoPS transcription omits that x_1 is a positive integer. This condition is explicit in the inspected Chinese paper reproduction and is restored.

cn.2025.2.6.text: The inspected SM International Education paper reproduction confirms n>=4 and the n^(-3/2) improvement, matching AoPS. A separate Beijing information-site transcription has a garbled formula and n>=3 and was not used for this problem.

Cyprus-pancyprian-problems.json.verification_notes: Nineteen complete Grade 12 examinations from the official CMS archive: December 2006, 2007, 2009–2019, February and December 2021, and December 2022–2025. School-year labels are converted to the actual examination year; 2021 has two examinations (day 1 February, day 2 December). The 2006 source gives December 2006–07, not an exact day. Pre-2006, 2008, and missing senior selection papers remain open; no standalone 2020 examination has been established. Editorial qualifications are displayed for 2015 P4, 2016 P2 and 2018 P3.

cy.2015.0.4.text: The official paper gives only four initial terms and an ellipsis, without a general rule. These do not uniquely determine a continuation or a largest term; the statement is retained with this source qualification.

cy.2016.0.2.text: The official paper prints a strict inequality. At a=b=1 both sides equal 64. The displayed inequality uses >=; equality is possible. This editorial correction is not an exact-source verification.

cy.2018.0.3.text: The official statement omits the necessary orientation AB<CD; its accompanying solution explicitly states this condition. It has been added here. No exact-source badge is assigned.

Other absent historical test labels and national archive retrieval outcomes are documented in docs/cyprus-pancyprian-2026-10-11.md. grj.1999.0.3.text: Source ambiguity: the bank text does not say where the point $E_1$ lies; by symmetry with $D_1$ it is presumably a point of side $BC$ (so that $CE_1=AC-CE=AE$). No official paper was found to confirm this.

grj.2000.0.4.text: Source ambiguity: as transcribed in the bank, the statement sets no limit on the number of books each student buys, so the requested maximum is not determined by the text; the official paper was not found.

grj.2001.0.4.text: Source note: The point called $\Theta$ in the Greek text is named $T$ here.

grj.2003.0.3.text: Source ambiguity: as transcribed in the bank, the construction of $S$ is impossible, since the perpendicular to $\varepsilon$ at $M$ is parallel to $AB$. In the intended configuration (a rhombus $AMBS$ whose diagonal $AB$ is perpendicular to $MS$) the point $S$ lies on $\varepsilon$, e.g. as the intersection of $\varepsilon$ with the perpendicular to $BC$ at $B$; the official paper was not found, so the text is kept as in the source. The point called $\Sigma$ in the Greek text is named $S$ here.

grj.2005.0.1.text: Source ambiguity: the bank text defines $K$ as the intersection of the lines $D\Lambda$ and $CB$, which is circular ($\Lambda$ is defined through $K$); it has been read as the intersection of the legs $DA$ and $CB$, the only reading consistent with parts (b) and (c). The official paper was not found. The point called $\Lambda$ in the Greek text is named $L$ here.

grj.2005.0.4.text: Editorial correction (no official paper found): the bank text asks for points $B,\Gamma,\Lambda$ on the circle but then speaks of the quadrilateral $AB\Gamma\Delta$; the third point is read as $D$ ($\Delta$). The circle and the vertex share the name $C$ as in the source (where they are $C$ and $\Gamma$).

grj.2007.0.1.text: Source ambiguity: the bank text speaks of "the circumcircle $C$ of the triangle $B\Gamma$" (a vertex is missing); it has been read as the circle through $B$, $I$, $C$, which is the reading consistent with the condition $N\neq I$. The official paper was not found.

grj.2009.0.4.text: Source note: The points called $\Pi$ (square) and $\Sigma$ (school) in the Greek text and figure are named $P$ and $S$ here.

il.1990.0.6.text: Editorial domain clarification: n >= 3 is required for a set of n points not all collinear. The published historical wording says every natural n.

il.1993.0.4.text: The institutional historical source itself warns that the proposed inequality is false and requests a counterexample instead. The English statement preserves that instruction; no correction of the proposed inequality is guessed.

il.1994.0.5.text: Editorial domain clarification: the vector (a1,...,an) is assumed nonzero so its displayed normalisation exists. The historical source does not state this restriction explicitly.

il.2017.0.4.text: Editorial domain correction: the printed statement permits x=0, p=-1, for which its parametrisation is impossible. The condition (x,p) != (0,-1) is added explicitly; this record does not receive an exact-source badge.

il.1983.0.5.text: Editorial hypothesis: the forest is assumed to be an open simply connected region. Without a no-holes assumption, an arbitrarily thin forest can contain the whole of any finite prescribed route, so the printed area-only guarantee is not justified. The historical source does not state this hypothesis explicitly; no original-source badge is assigned.

il.1983.0.9.text: The circle chain is taken in the upper semicircle, with distinct successive circles, as depicted in the published source figure. This rules out going back to the previously used tangent circle; the printed verbal recurrence alone does not state this choice explicitly.

il.1984.0.2.text: Editorial domain clarification: c > 0 is stated explicitly. The historical text calls c irrational but omits positivity; with c negative its displayed finite-sum identity need not hold.

il.1984.0.3.text: Intersections are assumed to exist, as required by the construction. The dependence on X,A,B,C,D is retained exactly; only independence from H,K is claimed.

il.1984.0.6.text: Editorial domain clarification: a != 0, since the displayed expression contains x/a^2.

il.1985.0.2.text: The published suggestion to use x log x >= x-1 is omitted to retain statements only, without a hint.

il.1986.0.7.text: The plane is outside the interior of the parallelepiped, and intersections are on the rays from A, consistent with the published figure and the volume-minimisation construction.

il.1988.0.4.text: The intersection M is considered only when the lines BB′ and CC′ are defined and meet; the zero rotation is excluded implicitly by this construction.

il.2014.0.6.text: Editorial domain correction: n >= 2 replaces positive n. At n=1 the minimum in the displayed formula is zero, so every real k works and there is no maximal real k. No exact-source badge is assigned to this corrected statement.

il.2018.0.3.text: Editorial domain clarification: a,b,c are not all zero, so the displayed denominator is nonzero. No exact-source badge is assigned.

il.2025.0.6.text: The second radical follows the corrected restatement in the official solutions publication (page 5): its numerator is bc+ab+1. The standalone question sheet has the typographical numerator bc+ca+1. The positive-real domain in the official publication is restored; the previous AoPS-derived record said non-negative.

ilg.2008.0.7.text: Editorial variable correction: the official paper prints F(x) < a for every rational a, with x unbound. The bank uses F(a) < a, matching the variable quantified in that clause. This is an editorial restoration, not an official erratum.

ilg.2009.0.4.text: The Hebrew phrase that each set contains 502 (respectively 251) points is translated as at least that many points; it does not assert that the sets have exactly those cardinalities.

ilg.2009.0.6.text: Editorial domain clarification: every club must have at least one member in both parts. The source explicitly states this in part (b), but omits it in part (a); allowing empty clubs makes part (a) false.

ilg.2010.0.3.text: Editorial degeneracy clarification: angles of 0 degrees are allowed. The source says acute angles without excluding collinear point sets; a strictly positive-angle reading fails for a collinear set.

ilg.2011.0.6.text: The initial statement on page 2 uses 10^20 - 1. The authors explicitly replace it with 10^20 - 9 on page 3. The bank follows that official corrected restatement.

ilg.2013.0.6.text: The official statement does not specify a starting point on an extended side line or the orientation of each associated line direction. Its wording is retained; the region construction is understood where it is defined. Source comparison does not certify these omitted boundary conventions.

ilg.2021.0.8.text: Editorial domain clarification: n >= 3 is required because the question asks for three distinct points. The official question omits a range for n. All ten answer expressions are retained. Their ordering changes for small n; the source does not specify a uniform or asymptotic comparison, which remains a source ambiguity.

ilg.2025.0.5.text: Editorial metric clarification: distance is measured along the shorter arc of the circle. The official statement does not explicitly define the metric; the official publication uses the circumference-based distance in its discussion.

ilg.2026.0.4.text: Editorial success-case clarification: when Daniel confirms the proposed ranking, the task is finished; elimination of m/(2n) other candidates is required only for a disagreement response. The original final sentence demands elimination without stating this exception. The official publication treats confirmation as success.

jpjp.2004.0.11.text: Source note: The official item is a fill-in-the-blanks dialogue (teacher and two students) that leads to the result, with blanks ア–ク to be filled. Only the underlying question is stored here (statements only, no solution text); the final blank asks for this number.

Only the problem is stored (statements only, no solution text). 'Subtracted without borrowing' (繰り下がりなしで引き算できる) means that, written with three digits (leading zeros allowed), the larger can be reduced by the smaller digit by digit with no borrow.

kgca.2011.0.26.text: Editorial correction: the paper prints "$\angle ABC = 75$" without the degree sign; the degree sign is supplied.

kgca.2007.0.18.text: Editorial correction: the source prints 'W, X ir Y' (Lithuanian 'ir' = 'and'); rendered as 'W, X and Y'.

kgca.2008.0.9.text: Source note: Amounts are in litas (Lithuanian currency of the source version).

kgec.2012.0.8.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper prints choice (B) as "on 21th of February"; written here as "21st".

kgec.2012.0.17.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper prints "the 22th step"; written here as "the 22nd step".

kgec.2013.0.1.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper prints "white kangaroes"; written here as "kangaroos".

kgec.2013.0.16.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper prints "greather than 21"; written here as "greater".

kgec.2014.0.13.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper prints "not on thepile"; written here as "not on the pile".

kgec.2014.0.19.text: Editorial correction: in the reference paper choice (C) is typeset broken ("(C" with ")4" displaced); the value 4 is confirmed by Cyprus and Canada.

kgec.2015.0.23.text: Source ambiguity: the reference paper (Pakistan, 'KSF 2015 - selected problems Ecolier') prints 'a shark, a cat and a rhino' with a cat drawing; Cyprus, Austria (Q23, two animals) and Canada (Q22) all have a pig, so the pig version is taken as the KSF text, with text and figure from Cyprus. The mathematics is the same.

kgec.2016.0.6.text: Editorial correction: the reference prints 'frieds'; corrected to 'friends'.

kgec.2016.0.21.text: Source ambiguity: the reference paper (Pakistan, 2016 Ecolier) prints a different problem as Q21 (basketball: 72 shots, 99 points, 30 two-point and 12 one-point baskets; total number of failed shots; choices 21, 16, 5, 50, 51). Cyprus (Q21) and Austria (Q21) both have this bowls problem, so it is taken as the KSF Q21, with text and figure from Cyprus; Canada's selection contains neither problem.

kgec.2017.0.3.text: Editorial correction: the reference prints 'slided'; corrected to 'slid'.

kgec.2017.0.6.text: Source ambiguity: the national versions disagree on the numbers. The reference (Pakistan) and Canada show 11 in the visible cell of the second row, with choices 10, 12, 13, 15, 16; Cyprus and Austria show 10 there, with choices 10, 11, 12, 13, 15. The reference version is kept.

kgec.2017.0.15.text: Source ambiguity: the reference paper (Pakistan) prints this stove problem as Q20 and has at Q15 a different problem ('Which of the routes is the longest?', five routes A–E drawn on a grid), which appears in none of the other national papers. Cyprus (Q15), Austria (Q15) and Canada (Q16) have the stove problem here, so the KSF order is followed; the text is taken from the reference paper's Q20.

kgec.2017.0.16.text: Source ambiguity: the reference paper (Pakistan) draws the cycle with the question mark after the '+4' step (answer 13) and choices 10, 11, 12, 13, 14. Cyprus and Austria both draw it with the question mark after the '−15' step, as here; Cyprus gives choices 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and Austria 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. The Cyprus/Austria drawing is taken as the KSF version, with the Cyprus choices and figure; Canada's selection omits the problem.

kgec.2017.0.20.text: Source ambiguity: the reference paper (Pakistan) has the stove problem at Q20 (see Q15) and lacks this problem. It is taken from Cyprus (Q20), confirmed by Austria (Q22) and Canada (Q21), which ask about tours visiting exactly two different animals.

kgec.2019.0.7.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper prints 'than Ria has' in the question; corrected to Pia, the name used in the first sentence of the same problem (and in the Cyprus and Canada versions).

kgec.2019.0.21.text: Source ambiguity: the Austria and Canada versions print the choices 2, 3, 4, 10, 18; the reference and Cyprus papers print 2, 3, 4, 8, 10 (kept).

kgec.2019.0.23.text: Source ambiguity: the reference paper orders the choices Alek, Darek, Czarek, Bartek, Edek; the Cyprus and Canada versions order them Alek, Bartek, Czarek, Darek, Edek (the order of the names in the statement), which is used here.

kgec.2020.0.18.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper prints choice (E) as 'chocolate with a wafer', a duplicate of (D); corrected to 'vanilla with a chocolate chip' as in the Saudi Mawhiba, Canada, Sweden and Cyprus versions.

kgec.2022.0.19.text: Source ambiguity: the Saudi booklet prints choice (E) as 80 cm in its English line (90 cm in its Arabic line); Cyprus, Sweden and Austria have 90 cm, which is used.

kgec.2025.0.12.text: Source ambiguity: choice (A) reads '1, 3' in the Saudi Mawhiba copy but '1 and 2' in the Cyprus and Austrian copies; the majority reading is given.

kgec.2026.0.4.text: Source ambiguity: the Swedish NCM copy (reworded, choices labelled differently) has (E) 8, while the Cyprus and Austrian copies have (E) 9; the majority reading is given.

kgec.2026.0.16.text: Source ambiguity: the Cyprus paper asks which ice cream Helen (the girl with the smallest amount) buys, whereas the Swedish NCM and Austrian copies ask about the third girl (Frans, resp. Clara), whose answer is a different picture choice; the question of the two concurring copies is used.

kgec.2005.0.1.text: Source note: The covered place is printed as a picture of a butterfly (see the figure).

kgec.2005.0.19.text: Editorial correction: 'seven boy' and 'three-digital number' corrected to 'seven boys' and 'three-digit number'.

kgec.2008.0.14.text: Source note: Choices (A)-(D) are printed as small pictures of the shapes (cross, triangle, square, cross and triangle); they are named in words here and also visible in the figure.

kgec.2008.0.15.text: Editorial correction: the source prints 'ia a hotel to host 21 guest'; typos corrected to 'in a hotel to host 21 guests'.

kgec.2010.0.4.text: Source note: Prices in Lt (litas): Lithuanian localisation of the currency in the source version.

kgj.2012.0.1.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper prints "an an isoceles triangle"; the doubled article and the spelling are corrected.

kgj.2012.0.3.text: Source ambiguity: the Pakistan IKMC Junior paper prints a four-piece variant (a $4\times2\times2$ cuboid made of four pieces, the same problem as in the KSF Ecolier paper and the Pakistan Cadet paper). The Junior papers of Cyprus and Austria both print this three-piece version ($3\times2\times2$ cuboid, same five choice drawings), which is taken here as the KSF Junior problem; text and figure from the Cyprus paper.

kgj.2012.0.5.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper's text says "The square $ABCE$ ... the distance from the point $D$ to the line $g$" and choice (E) "Depends on the location of $D$", which contradicts its own figure (square $ABCD$ with $E$ outside it) and the triangle $ECD$. The labels are corrected to the figure, as in the Austrian and Canadian versions (square $ABCD$, distance from $E$).

kgj.2012.0.8.text: Source ambiguity: the Cyprus and Austria Junior papers print instead the computation problem "To the number 6 we add 3 ..." (also the KSF Benjamin/Cadet problem), while the Canadian grade 9-10 paper prints a variant of this replace-each-8 problem; the reference (Pakistan) problem is kept.

kgj.2013.0.14.text: Source ambiguity: the order of the last two choices differs between national versions: the reference (Pakistan) paper prints (D) 60, (E) 50; the Cyprus paper (D) 50, (E) 60; the Canadian paper lists 60, 50, 40, 30, 20; the Austrian paper (D) 60% and (E) "too little information". The reference order is kept.

kgj.2014.0.5.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper prints "bigger then"; corrected to "bigger than".

kgj.2014.0.19.text: Source note: The reference paper (and the Cyprus paper) spells the third sister both "Hannah" and "Hanna"; kept as printed.

kgj.2015.0.11.text: Source ambiguity: the reference paper adds the editorial remark "[Possible to take away first die on the picture!]" after the question; it is omitted here. The reference, Cyprus and Austrian papers show three dice, while the Canadian version shows the die in two positions.

kgj.2016.0.23.text: Source ambiguity: the Pakistan paper prints a different problem as Q23 (shaded square in a 3 x 3 grid); this KSF Q23 follows the Cyprus paper, whose choices 11, 12, 13, 14, 15 agree with the Austrian paper; the Canadian version prints the choices 10, 12, 13, 14, 24.

kgj.2019.0.16.text: Source ambiguity: choice (E) reads 'The whole concentrate' in the Cyprus paper and 'All of the concentrate.' in the Canadian English paper; the Cyprus wording is kept.

kgj.2020.0.20.text: Source note: Editorial: the Pakistan paper prints 'six trangles meet'; the typo is corrected to 'triangles'.

kgj.2021.0.12.text: Source ambiguity: the walker's name differs between the national English versions (Pakistan IKMC: Ahmad; Cyprus: Andreas; Saudi Mawhiba: Faisal); the problem is not in the Canadian or Swedish selections, so the KSF name could not be confirmed. The Pakistan reference name is kept.

kgj.2021.0.21.text: Editorial correction: the Pakistan IKMC paper prints choice (E) as $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{32}$, a typographical error; the Saudi Mawhiba, Cyprus and Swedish versions all print $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$, which is used here.

kgj.2025.0.6.text: Source ambiguity: choice (E) is 12 in the Saudi Mawhiba copy but 11 in the Swedish NCM, Austrian and Cyprus English copies; the majority reading 11 is given.

kgj.2025.0.7.text: Source ambiguity: choice (E) is printed $157^\circ$ in the Saudi Mawhiba copy but $157.5^\circ$ in the Swedish NCM, Austrian and Cyprus copies; the majority reading is given.

kgj.2025.0.20.text: Source ambiguity: the Saudi Mawhiba copy prints the choices in the reverse order ((A) $\frac18$, (B) $\frac16$, (C) $\frac15$, (D) $\frac14$, (E) $\frac13$); the Swedish NCM, Austrian and Cyprus copies have (A) $\frac13$ ... (E) $\frac18$, which is given here.

kgj.2026.0.17.text: Source ambiguity: Ernest's statement is "I did not come fourth" in the Swedish NCM English copy, but "I didn't finish" in the Austrian copy and "I didn't make it to the finish line" in Cyprus; the Cyprus/Austria reading is given.

kgj.2005.0.18.text: Source ambiguity: the Austrian version asks instead how many different totals of passing buses Lisa can count during her 19-minute wait (same choices); the Estonian wording (difference of the two counts) is used here. Translated from the Estonian Kangaroo paper (University of Tartu Teaduskool, Russian-language version) (Q12); the problem also appears in the Austrian Q12.

kgj.2005.0.19.text: Source note: Translated from the Estonian Kangaroo paper (University of Tartu Teaduskool, Russian-language version) (Q13); the problem also appears in the Austrian Q18.

kgj.2005.0.20.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper prints "$BAC>60^\circ$" without the angle sign; $\angle BAC$ is meant.

kgj.2005.0.21.text: Source note: Translated from the Estonian Kangaroo paper (University of Tartu Teaduskool, Russian-language version) (Q22); the problem also appears in the Austrian Q23.

kgj.2005.0.22.text: Source note: Translated from the Estonian Kangaroo paper (University of Tartu Teaduskool, Russian-language version) (Q26); the problem also appears in the Austrian Q22.

kgj.2005.0.28.text: Source note: Translated from the Estonian Kangaroo paper (University of Tartu Teaduskool, Russian-language version) (Q29); the problem also appears in the Austrian Q26.

kgj.2005.0.29.text: Source ambiguity: the Austrian version (fish laid out with ten matches) has the choices $\sqrt{2}$, $\sqrt{3}$, 2, $\sqrt{5}$, $\sqrt{6}$; the Estonian choices are used here, as the figure is taken from that paper. Translated from the Estonian Kangaroo paper (University of Tartu Teaduskool, Russian-language version) (Q30); the problem also appears in the Austrian Q28.

kgj.2006.0.10.text: Source ambiguity: the Austrian version has the choices 7, 8, 9, 10, 11; the Estonian choices are used here, as the figure is taken from that paper. Translated from the Estonian Kangaroo paper (University of Tartu Teaduskool, Russian-language version) (Q8); the problem also appears in the Austrian Q12.

kgj.2006.0.11.text: Source note: Translated from the Austrian Kangaroo paper (German) (Q19); the problem also appears in the Estonian Q20.

kgj.2006.0.18.text: Source ambiguity: the Austrian version of this problem has different choices ((A) always less than 99, ... (E) none of the properties A to D must hold); the choices of the reference paper are kept.

kgj.2006.0.22.text: Source note: Translated from the Estonian Kangaroo paper (University of Tartu Teaduskool, Russian-language version) (Q28); the problem also appears in the Austrian Q28.

kgj.2006.0.25.text: Source note: Translated from the Estonian Kangaroo paper (University of Tartu Teaduskool, Russian-language version) (Q29); the problem also appears in the Austrian Q29.

kgj.2006.0.26.text: Source ambiguity: the Austrian version lists the same five numbers in the order 17, 13, 20, 14, 9; the Estonian order is used here. Translated from the Estonian Kangaroo paper (University of Tartu Teaduskool, Russian-language version) (Q30); the problem also appears in the Austrian Q30.

kgj.2006.0.27.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper begins "Aslam's family consists of ..." (a Pakistan localisation) but asks about "the Dobson family"; the name Dobson from the question sentence is used in both places.

kgj.2007.0.16.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper says that the amount of petrol per km is "inversely proportional" to the velocity and sets the problem at 9:00 AM with choices 10:12 AM to 10:50 AM; the Canadian, Austrian and Estonian papers all have consumption proportional to the velocity, the time 21:00 and the choices 22:12, 22:15, 22:20, 22:25, 22:30 (Canada: E other answer), which are used here.

kgj.2007.0.18.text: Source ambiguity: the Canadian paper prints the choice (C) as 45 cm; the Austrian and Estonian papers both have 40 cm, which is used here.

kgj.2007.0.19.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper omits the question sentence (its choices are "10 Matches" ... "50 Matches"); the question "How many matches does each student play?" is restored from the Austrian and Estonian papers.

kgj.2007.0.22.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper prints choice (D) as $6+12\pi/6$; the Canadian, Austrian and Estonian papers have $6+2\pi$.

kgj.2007.0.23.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper prints choice (B) as $S_3=\frac{S_1\times S_2}{2}$; the Canadian, Austrian and Estonian papers have $S_3=\frac{S_1+S_2}{2}$.

kgj.2007.0.27.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper has only three colours (3 green, 3 yellow and 3 blue cards) and choice (E) "Another answer"; the Canadian, Austrian and Estonian papers all have four colours (three cards of each of four colours) and choice (E) "the four events have the same probability", which are used here.

kgj.2007.0.30.text: Source note: Translated from the Estonian Kangaroo paper (University of Tartu Teaduskool, Russian-language version) (Q30); the problem also appears in the Austrian Q30.

kgj.2008.0.2.text: Source note: The reference paper says "under half of the minute" and "under the hundredth part of one hour"; the Austrian and Estonian papers state that the runners took half a minute and one hundredth of an hour respectively, which is used here.

kgj.2008.0.7.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper prints only "Each letter is a digit, a digit is only one letter, which digit is K?" without the letter sum; the addition $OK+KO=WOW$ is restored from the Austrian paper.

kgj.2008.0.18.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper's choices (260, 510, 520, 1020, 130) do not contain the correct value; choice (C) 746 is taken from the Estonian paper (the other four choices agree), and 746 also appears among the Austrian choices.

kgj.2008.0.24.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper states only "Perimeter [arc] = ?" next to the figure; the wording (three touching circles with radii 1, 2, 3; length of the bold arc of the smallest circle) is completed from the Estonian and Austrian versions.

kgj.2008.0.27.text: Source note: The reference paper says "(see the fig.)" but prints no figure; the reference to the figure is omitted.

kgj.2009.0.23.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper's choices (21, 22, 23, 24, 25) do not contain the correct value; the choices 14, 16, 20, 24, 25 of the Austrian paper are used (the Estonian paper has 12, 13, 14, 15, 16).

kgj.2010.0.8.text: Source ambiguity: the Austrian paper asks for $1+3+5+\ldots+17+19$ and the Estonian paper for $1+3+5+\ldots+19+21$, both with the choices $10\times10$, $11\times11$, $12\times12$, $13\times13$, $14\times14$; the version of the reference paper is kept.

kgj.2010.0.25.text: Source ambiguity: the Austrian paper adds the condition that no two segments may intersect and has the choices 10, 11, 12, 13, infinitely many; the reference version is kept.

kgj.2011.0.10.text: Source note: The reference paper has no figure for this problem; the figure (three stacked dice) is taken from the Austrian paper, whose question asks for the number of pips on the face marked X (the top face of the top die).

kgj.2011.0.24.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper's choices (A) and (B) say "on the same side of L as A", but no point A is defined; $W$ (as in the Austrian version, where the tetrahedron is $ABCD$) is meant.

kgpe.2012.0.13.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper prints "then he cuts 1 off head again" (also Cyprus); written here as "then he cuts off 1 head again" (Canada: "then he cuts off one more head").

kgpe.2014.0.4.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper prints "animials"; written here as "animals".

kgpe.2014.0.13.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper prints "lenght"; written here as "length".

kgpe.2014.0.16.text: Source note: the reference paper prints a leftover editorial placeholder line "New diagram required." below the pelican diagram; the diagram itself (three pelicans with speech bubbles) is printed and is used; the placeholder is omitted.

kgpe.2016.0.9.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper omits the full stop after "as in the picture"; it is added.

kgpe.2016.0.16.text: Editorial correction: the reference paper prints "What will be sum of their ages"; "the" is added (as in Cyprus).

kgpe.2016.0.23.text: Source ambiguity: the Cyprus text lists filled diamond and heart symbols while its picture shows outline ones; the outline forms are used, matching the picture. Austria Felix 2016 Q15 has the same problem with different symbols.

kgpe.2017.0.2.text: Source ambiguity: Cyprus prints a different, overlapping arrangement of stars; the reference arrangement (also in Canada 2017 Q4) is kept.

kgpe.2017.0.6.text: Source ambiguity: Cyprus and Austria print the choices 8, 9, 10, 11, 12; the reference choices 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 (also Canada 2017 Q3) are kept.

kgpe.2017.0.10.text: Source ambiguity: Cyprus and Austria (Felix 2017 Q6) order the picture choices differently (their (A) and (C) are the reference (C) and (A)); the reference order is kept.

kgpe.2017.0.12.text: Source ambiguity: Cyprus and Austria say ten turns (same final position), and Cyprus swaps choices (D) and (E); the reference (six turns, also Canada 2017 Q8) is kept.

kgpe.2017.0.15.text: Source ambiguity: Cyprus prints "a quarter past one" with a different clock and different clock choices; the reference version (also Canada 2017 Q9) is kept.

kgpe.2017.0.22.text: Source ambiguity: Cyprus and Austria draw the keys in the order 141, 717, 417, 471; the reference order 141, 471, 417, 717 (also Canada 2017 Q13) is kept (same answer).

kgpe.2017.0.23.text: Source ambiguity: this problem is attested at Pre-Ecolier level only by Cyprus (it is also KSF Ecolier 2017 Q2); the reference paper has the fruit problem (KSF Q13) at Q23 and a national dice problem at Q13, so the KSF Q23 is taken from Cyprus.

kgpe.2018.0.7.text: Source ambiguity: Canada (grade 1-2 Q6, same five towers and the same five choices) asks for tower number 6. Cyprus's 'figure number 16' is kept: the Math Kangaroo USA 2018 answer key for Levels 1-2 gives (E) for Q7, which is the 16th tower in this choice set (the 6th would be (B)).

kgpe.2019.0.9.text: Editorial correction: typo 'cannott' in the Pakistan paper corrected to 'cannot' (Cyprus, Canada).

kgpe.2019.0.11.text: Source ambiguity: the Pakistan paper prints choices (A) 5-3-2-1-4 and (D) 5-2-3-1-4; Canada (Q11) prints them in the opposite positions. The correct order 5-2-3-1-4 is (A) in the Math Kangaroo USA 2019 answer key for Levels 1-2 (Q11: A), so the Canadian/USA choice order is used.

kgpe.2020.0.17.text: Editorial correction: typo 'countains' in the Pakistan paper corrected to 'contains'.

kgpe.2021.0.21.text: Source ambiguity: this question is printed only in the Cyprus paper; Pakistan has instead (as its Q4) a different problem (Michael's toy shelf: which of five shelves has neither turtles, rabbits nor brown teddy bears), and no third English copy of the full 2021 Pre-Ecolier paper (Saudi, Sweden, Austria) was available to decide which one is the KSF problem.

kgpe.2022.0.2.text: Editorial correction: the Pakistan scan prints choice (B) as a copy of choice (A); figure taken from the Cyprus paper, whose choice (B) (left half of the mushroom next to a rotated right half) agrees with the Austrian Felix 2022 paper.

kgpe.2023.0.23.text: Source ambiguity: the national versions disagree on the last two questions. Pakistan (Q23 apples, Q24 frogs) and the Austrian Felix grade-2 paper (apples then frogs as its last two questions) agree, and the Canadian grades 1-2 paper also contains the apple problem; Cyprus has frogs as Q23 and a digit-card subtraction problem as Q24 (Canada has an addition variant). The Pakistan order is kept.

kgpe.2024.0.17.text: Source ambiguity: in the Cyprus paper the small white marker square appears only on the top of the cube in the main drawing, while the Austrian version (Felix 2024 Q9/Q11) also draws it in the top-left cell of every answer choice to fix the orientation; the Cyprus drawing is kept.

kgpe.2025.0.9.text: Editorial correction: Cyprus prints 'not touching a rubber hand'; corrected to 'rubber band' (Greek text and Austrian version: rubber bands).

kgpe.2025.0.23.text: Editorial correction: Cyprus prints '4 squared red'; corrected to '4 squares red'.

kgpe.2026.0.4.text: Source ambiguity: Cyprus prints (D) 9; Sweden and Austria both have (D) 12, used here.

kgpe.2026.0.5.text: Source ambiguity: the Swedish version (Milou 2026 Q5) has choices 4, 5, 6, 9, 12; Cyprus choices 3, 6, 9, 12, 15 kept (no third version available).

kgpe.2026.0.6.text: Editorial correction: the Cyprus English text names the child 'Paul' in the first sentence and 'Bernard' in the second; one name (Bernard, as in the Austrian 'Bernhard') used throughout.

kgpe.2026.0.24.text: Source note: Editorial: the Cyprus-only localisation 'In Nicosia,' at the start is omitted (absent from the Austrian version).

kgs.2013.0.20.text: Source note: Editorial: the reference (Pakistan IKMC) copy prints the name as "Franois" (the c-cedilla was lost in typesetting); restored to "François".

kgs.2013.0.23.text: Source note: Choices (A)–(D) are pictures and choice (E) is text; the figure shows the cube and the four picture choices.

kgs.2014.0.17.text: Source note: The question asks for $x$, while the figure labels the vertex with a capital X.

kgs.2014.0.28.text: Source note: The choices are printed without degree signs in the reference paper; kept as printed.

kgs.2016.0.22.text: Editorial correction: the Pakistan IKMC paper prints choice (B) as "$3\sqrt{2} : x$" (a font error for $\pi$); $3\sqrt{2} : \pi$ is restored as in the Austrian English version of the same problem.

kgs.2016.0.29.text: Source note: Source substitution in the reference: the Pakistan IKMC 2016 paper has a national question 29 (remainders of $(n+1)^3$ divided by $n^3$). The KSF question 29 (this chessboard problem) is taken from the Cyprus paper, which agrees with the Austrian English version of the same problem.

kgs.2018.0.5.text: Source ambiguity: the national English/translated copies of this KSF problem differ in the choices: Canada (used here) prints 11, 7, 8, 9, 10; Austria prints 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 (both with 12 cubes and the same 12-cube drawing). Cyprus prints a 10-cube variant with choices 6–10.

kgs.2021.0.18.text: Source note: Editorial: the two crossing types are separate small pictures inside the sentence ('like this: [picture] or like this: [picture]'); they are reproduced side by side below the knot in the figure, and the bracketed references were added to the text.

kgs.2022.0.1.text: Source note: Name: the Saudi Mawhiba booklet localises the name ('Hashem'); the KSF name Henry is used (as in the Cyprus paper). The Pakistan IKMC 2022 paper replaces this question with a national problem, so the Saudi booklet is the reference for Q1.

kgs.2024.0.28.text: Source ambiguity: choice (E) is "none of the previous" in the Saudi Mawhiba copy (also Cyprus; Austria "another number"), but "42" in the Swedish NCM English copy of the KSF paper. The Saudi reading is kept.

kgs.2025.0.14.text: Source ambiguity: choice (E) is printed $\frac{\pi}{3r}$ in the Saudi Mawhiba copy but $\frac{\pi}{2r}$ in the Swedish NCM and Austrian English copies and in Cyprus; the majority reading $\frac{\pi}{2r}$ is given.

kgs.2025.0.15.text: Source ambiguity: choice (E) is "none of the previous" in the Saudi Mawhiba copy (also Cyprus; Austria "an other number"), but $2^4 \cdot 3^6$ in the Swedish NCM English copy. The Saudi reading is kept.

kgs.2025.0.18.text: Source ambiguity: the Saudi Mawhiba copy prints choice (E) as "none-negative" (Arabic: non-negative), whereas the Swedish NCM ("None of the other options are true"), Austrian ("None of these four statements is definitely true") and Cyprus copies have "none of the others is always true"; the majority reading is given.

kgs.2026.0.6.text: Source note: The Austrian national version of this problem uses underwear instead of socks and different choices (A) €6.00 and (E) €8.40; the Swedish English version agrees with the Cyprus choices.

kgs.2026.0.10.text: Editorial correction: the Cyprus paper (English and Greek lines) prints the condition as "α = (b/c)²" with a Greek alpha; the digit $a$ of $\overline{abc}$ is meant, as in the Austrian and Swedish English versions of the same problem.

kgs.2026.0.17.text: Source note: Editorial: the Cyprus English text names the first point with a Greek alpha ("points α, b, c and d"); the figure labels it $a$, as do the Greek line of the same paper and the Swedish English version.

kgs.2026.0.27.text: Source note: The Swedish English version agrees with Cyprus (points on the edges of a cube); the Austrian national version places the nine points on the axes of a 3D coordinate system.

kgs.2026.0.28.text: Source note: Editorial: the Cyprus paper defines $a_n$ but writes the sum with Greek alphas ("α1 − α2 + … + α2025 − α2026"); the Latin $a_n$ is used throughout, as in the Austrian and Swedish English versions.

kgs.2005.0.16.text: Source ambiguity: the Pakistan IKMC paper prints choice (E) as a symbol-font character that does not render (its code is the Symbol-font nabla position); it is read here as the empty set $\emptyset$, the only sensible set-valued choice. Choice (C) is printed with $\cap$, as kept here.

kgs.2005.0.19.text: Editorial correction: choice (E) is printed "non of these" in the Pakistan IKMC paper; spelling corrected.

kgs.2006.0.16.text: Editorial correction: the Pakistan IKMC paper prints "Than the ratio"; corrected to "Then".

kgs.2007.0.6.text: Editorial correction: "Egytians" in the Pakistan IKMC paper corrected to "Egyptians".

kgs.2007.0.11.text: Source ambiguity: the Canada paper (Q9) asks instead for "the area of the region obtained by stretching a rubber band around the squares" (the convex hull), with the same choices; the Pakistan IKMC wording (area covered by at least one of the squares) is kept.

kgs.2007.0.12.text: Editorial correction: "greater then" in the Pakistan IKMC paper corrected to "greater than".

kz.2013.2.6.text: Editorial clarification: the AoPS and Matol statements say the turtles last met only at (0,0), although both finish at (n,n). The bank explicitly excludes meetings only at intermediate points. This interpretation is supported by the archived Matol solution discussion at https://matol.kz/comments/1028/show, which counts disjoint interior paths between the first and penultimate steps. The supporting discussion is a community solution, not an official wording correction.

lv.1994.0.4.text: Editorial correction: in the archive PDF (44repol_uzd.pdf) the right-hand side is printed garbled as 'm!1' (a symbol lost in conversion); the official solution in the same archive (44repol_atr.pdf, 44.19: the only solution is n=m=1, since 1!+...+n! is never a cube for n>=2) shows the intended right-hand side is m^3.

my.2020.0.2.text: Editorial correction: the official PDF starts the right-hand sum at 1/1011. The correct start is 1/1001. Separating the harmonic sum into its even and odd terms proves the correction; the printed formula omits ten positive terms. The corrected statement does not receive an exact-source check.

my.2022.0.6.text: Editorial clarification: S must be nonempty. The official sheet says every subset, but the empty subset gives zero points for every team and contradicts the stated odd-total hypothesis. The clarified statement does not receive an exact-source check.

my.2025.0.1.text: Unresolved source domain gap: the official sheet says only a <= 2025 and does not specify the domains of a and k or a lower bound for a. The bank preserves that wording without adding an unconfirmed target range. If arbitrarily negative integer targets are allowed, no finite uniform move bound is possible. Organizer clarification is needed; this statement receives no exact-source badge.

rio.2000.0.2.text: Source note: The OMA page writes $\geq$ as an underlined $>$ (HTML <u>></u>); read as $\geq$.

rio.2000.0.3.text: Source note: The OMA page writes $\geq$ and $\leq$ as underlined $>$ and $<$; read accordingly.

rio.2000.0.4.text: Editorial correction: the OMA page has OCR-type misprints ('(b + l)' for $(b+1)$, 'decirnal' for 'decimal').

rio.2000.0.5.text: Source note: The OMA page names the circle 'G' (a Greek Gamma lost in a Symbol-font conversion); written here as $\Gamma$. 'rnedio' (misprint) read as 'medio'.

rio.2000.0.6.text: Source note: The OMA page sets the function name in Symbol font ('j' = $\varphi$).

rio.2002.1.2.text: Source note: The OMA page renders $\lambda$ and $\geq$ in a lost Symbol font ('l', '³'); restored from the accompanying formula image, which shows $\lambda$.

rio.2002.2.5.text: Source note: The OMA page renders $\Gamma$ and $\neq$ in a lost Symbol font ('G', '¹').

rio.2003.1.3.text: Source note: The figure is cropped without its Spanish captions ('rectángulo 1 × 3', 'tetraminó en forma de T'), which are rendered in the text.

rio.2005.2.5.text: Source note: The OMA page renders the floor/absolute-value brackets in a lost Symbol font; read from context as $|S-100|$ (and $\lfloor\,\rfloor$ in P1).

rio.2010.2.4.text: Source note: As printed on the OMA page; the list $r_1, \ldots, r_{1000}$ has one more term than the divisors $2, \ldots, 1000$ (presumably $r_k$ is the remainder on division by $k$).

ro11.2003.0.2.text: Source note: Possible defect in the original: if some $a_i$ coincide (e.g. $a_1 = a_2$), two rows of $M$ are equal and $\det(M) = 0$; the solution in the source assumes $1 < b_1 < b_2 < b_3$, i.e. effectively strict inequalities $1 \le a_1 < a_2 < a_3 < a_4$. The printed statement is kept.

ro11.2003.0.4.text: Source note: The paper does not define $A^*$; in Romanian usage it is the adjugate of $A$ (as the solution confirms: $A A^* = A^* A = \det(A) I_3$).

ro11.2004.0.2.text: Source note: The paper uses the standard notation $[x]$ for the integer part of $x$ without defining it.

ro11.2010.0.3.text: Editorial correction: the official paper defines $g(x) = e^{-x} g(x)$; the solution in the same document uses $g(x) = e^{-x} f(x)$, which is clearly intended.

ro11.2012.0.1.text: Editorial correction: the official paper writes $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}$, although $f$ and $g$ are defined on $[0,1]$; read as $[0,1]$.

ro12.2003.0.3.text: Editorial correction: the scanned statement prints the hypothesis as $x(f) \ge \int_0^x f(t)\,dt$; the solution in the same document uses $xf(x) \ge \int_0^x f(t)\,dt$, which is clearly intended.

ro12.2010.0.2.text: Source note: The Romanian word corp (field) is rendered as division ring, following SSMR usage, where a corp need not be commutative.

ro12.2011.0.4.text: Source note: Notation of the paper: $F'_s$ and $F'_d$ are the left and right derivatives (Romanian stânga/dreapta).

ro12.2012.0.3.text: Editorial correction: in (a) the paper writes $f(x) = x$ for $a < x \le 1$; read as $f_a(x) = x$.

ro12.2023.0.2.text: Source note: The paper writes the binomial coefficient as $C_m^k$ (Romanian notation); rendered here as $\binom{m}{k}$.

es.1975.1.3.text: Source ambiguity: both available sources (the SCM booklet compiled from the Gaceta Matemática, and the Jaén archive) give as 1975 P3 exactly the statement of 1974 P3; the repetition could not be checked against an original paper. es.1979.2.8.text: Source ambiguity: the Jaén archive prints 5x^3+7x^5, which is inconsistent with the last term 1001x^500; the SCM booklet has 5x^2+7x^3 (coefficient 2k+1 of x^k), which is followed.

es.1982.1.1.text: Source ambiguity: the Jaén archive ends with "indicate how this problem would be solved mathematically"; the SCM booklet asks to analyse the given solution and say what a mathematician would do; the latter is followed.

th.2004.1.8.text: Source ambiguity: the retrieved English paper prints 2x + 4x + 2547. This is reproduced literally; no missing exponent or correction is inferred.

th.2004.2.22.text: Incomplete source condition: the retrieved English paper prints only “CA + AI + BC”, without a relation. This historical record is incomplete and must not be used as a complete exercise until an independent source restores the missing condition.

th.2007.1.13.text: Source ambiguity: the paper does not state whether the two selected subsets are ordered. The wording is preserved without imposing a convention.

th.2010.1.1.text: Source ambiguity: the paper does not state whether the balls are distinguishable. This is preserved rather than inventing a convention.

th.2014.2.7.text: Source endpoint omission: the paper excludes P = E but does not explicitly exclude endpoints that make the circumcircle APD degenerate. Its wording is preserved.

th.2016.2.7.text: Source omission: the paper does not explicitly specify the coefficient field. The printed statement is preserved; the real-coefficient assumption has not been silently added.

tht.2011.10.28.text: Editorial clarification: the source gives K_0 = 1 but prints the recurrence for n ≥ 0, which conflicts at zero. The recurrence is stated here for n ≥ 1; its conclusion still includes n = 0.

tht.2011.14.42.text: Source ambiguity: A_iA_jA_k is not defined. The source itself asks whether this denotes triangle area. The ratio is retained without inventing that convention.

tht.2012.9.25.text: Unresolved source error: the source prints “infinitely many” fixed-degree monic integer polynomials. That wording is reproduced literally, without an unverified correction. The printed assertion is defective; do not use this historical record as a valid exercise until an independent contest source resolves it.

tht.2012.9.26.text: Notation correction: the source switches its evaluation variable from t to k within the question. A single positive integer t is used consistently here.

tht.2013.1.2.text: Notation correction: condition (ii) quantifies n in the source, although its displayed variable is k. The quantifier here uses k.

tht.2013.3.7.text: Source ambiguity: the source footnote explicitly questions whether the conclusion is (i) or (ii), or both. The printed “either … or” is retained.

tht.2013.4.10.text: Potential source typo: the middle denominator is printed z(y+z)+x(y+z). This is retained literally without replacing it by a cyclic expression.

tht.2013.10.29.text: Potential source typo: the source prints |a_{i+1}−a_1|, not consecutive differences. Its condition is retained literally and has not been mathematically certified.

tht.2013.10.30.text: Convention clarification: the source uses N for the iteration parameter. Positive k is used here, since allowing k = 0 would trivialize the stated minimum.

tht.2014.4.13.text: Source omission: the source does not specify or quantify the parameter k. This omission remains unresolved; no range or fixed value is inferred.

tht.2014.7.24.text: Notation correction: the source calls O the circumcircle while using line OI. O is rendered as the circumcentre here, consistently with the construction.

tht.2015.8.27.text: Source convention omission: the infinite expansion is printed without explicitly requiring eventual zero digits or stating the meaning of its sum. The printed formulation is preserved.

tht.2018.1.3.text: Source ambiguity: the printed question does not specify the domain of the arithmetic progression or a convention for perfect powers. No additional domain has been invented.

tht.2018.6.17.text: Unresolved source error: the printed condition is AX = AU, but point U is never defined. The literal statement is retained. Do not use as a valid exercise until an independent contest source resolves the missing definition.

tht.2018.9.26.text: Unresolved source error: players choose only indices 1 through p−1, but the displayed number also contains a₀, whose value or choice is not specified. The literal statement is retained. Do not use as a valid exercise until an independent contest source resolves this omission.

tht.2019.4.10.text: Unresolved source error: the source prints starting position 2n and step 2n, while allowing n = 0 although positions are numbered from 1. No missing exponent or indexing convention has been inferred. This record requires an independent contest source before use.

tht.2019.8.23.text: Unresolved source error: the source prints 1 ≥ k ≥ n for n ≥ 2, an impossible range. This literal range is retained; do not use as a valid exercise until independently resolved.

tht.2020.8.22.text: Unresolved source error: the source introduces u₁ through u₂₀₁₉ but then uses u₁ through u_N for arbitrary N ≥ 2. The literal mismatch is retained. An independent contest source is needed to confirm the intended index range.

tht.2020.8.23.text: Source convention omission: the quantified coefficient choices include the zero polynomial, but the source does not specify whether its roots are excluded. No nonzero-polynomial condition has been added.

totj.1980.2.1.text: Source note: First Tournament ("Olympiad of three cities"), spring 1980: a single paper without level division, each problem marked with the grades it was intended for. Only the problems intended for the youngest grade (marked 8 or 8-10) are included; archive problem 4 (grades 9-10 only) is omitted, so the numbering differs from the archive from problem 4 on.

totj.1981.2.1.text: Source note: Second Tournament (1980-81 school year): a single round without level division into O/A papers; the archive gives no date, and the paper is stored under 1981 as the spring round by assumption (as in the senior row). Junior grades (7-8) paper.

totj.1982.1.1.text: Source note: First round of the 4th Tournament (1982-83; the archive gives no date; stored under 1982 as the autumn round, as in the senior row). Junior grades (7-8) paper; there was no level division into O/A papers.

totj.1983.1.5.text: Editorial correction: the archive text reads "N draughts" followed by the editors' remark "the condition contained an error - N^2"; the number $n^2$ (a draught on every cell) is used here. The board size is written $N$ in the statement and $n$ in the cases, unified here as $n$.

tot.1980.2.1.text: Source note: First Tournament ("Olympiad of three cities": Kiev, Moscow, Riga), spring 1980: a single paper without level division, each problem marked with the grades it was intended for. Only the problems for the senior grades (marked 8-10 or 9-10) are included; archive problem 3 (grade 8 only) is omitted, so the numbering differs from the archive from problem 3 on.

tot.1981.2.1.text: Source note: Second Tournament (1980-81 school year): a single round without level division; the archive gives no date, and the paper is stored under 1981 as the spring round by assumption. Senior grades (9-10) paper.

tot.1982.1.1.text: Source note: First round of the 4th Tournament (1982-83; the archive page heading says "1981-82 учебный год", the archive index says 1982-83). The archive gives no date for this round; it is stored under 1982 as the autumn round because the second round was held on 20 March 1983. The round had a single senior (grades 9-10) paper without level division.

tot.1982.1.2.text: Source note: The archive figure labels the vertex adjacent to A, F and G with the letter M, whereas the text calls it H; the figure is reproduced unchanged from the archive (GIF converted to PNG).

Usa-tst-problems.json.verification_notes: All 85 currently stored statements, across 14 selection cycles (2012–2026, excluding 2022), have been visually and textually compared with published exam copies. This does not certify that the archive includes every historical USA TST. Sources are exam copies hosted in Evan Chen’s archive, or the USA TST public archive for 2026. Year labels denote selection cycles; exams may start in December of the preceding calendar year. The 2012 PDF has an inconsistent 54th IMO header; its printed exam dates are December 15, 2011 and February 1, 2012. The 2025 Day II PDF prints January 9, 2024; this is recorded as a source-header inconsistency rather than silently changing the collection year.
